def.name: candidate-generator-consensus
def.description: Specialist panel reviews the proposed candidate-generator (explore half) design for the IRIS optimization loop; arbiter reports consensus or consolidated critique.

args.proposal:
IRIS optimization loop — CANDIDATE-GENERATOR v1 (explore half), FINAL consolidated r4. Measure half = locked eval DL-0022. Top-5 cap = DL-0020. Portable loop = DL-0021. Operational constants marked [tunable]; items marked OPEN are human-input decisions that DO NOT block the design lock.

PURPOSE: given a run's eval signal, propose candidate CHANGES to the agent stack, score them, rank them, emit top-5 for human-approved routing.

A. CANDIDATE TYPES + blast tier: (1) prompt/instruction — HIGH global prefix / MEDIUM lane-scoped suffix; MUST carry {target_prompt: sql_generation|findings_prose|system_prefix}; a findings_prose Type-1 is rejected at generation if the cluster's failures are all L1 (SQL-layer) — wrong layer. (2) reflections/habits(notes) — HIGH global / MEDIUM domain / LOW table|user; MUST carry {scope, scope_key}; 'landed' = merged+approved. (3) tool schema/description — MEDIUM. (4) retrieval-corpus content — EVAL-INVISIBLE (eval injects context directly; retrieval bypassed) → human-judgment queue, NOT suite-scored; metric-disambiguation failures surface as a distinct morning-report line (count+examples) — acknowledged v1 structural blind spot with zero closed-loop leverage [OPEN: accept for v1, roadmap a retrieval-path eval]. (5) routing/classifier code — HIGH, code PR. EXCLUDED: eval fixtures + judge prompts (meta firewall) → fixture-audit queue.

B. INPUT UNIT = FAILURE CLUSTER by (L2a failure-tag + domain + lane co-filter) + low L2b cases (flagged advisory-driven). L3 EXCLUDED until κ≥0.7. CLUSTERING PRIORITY: fabrication/omission cluster by query-pattern-tag first; attribution/required-fact-missing cluster by domain first. Cluster input: transcripts, executed rows, failure tags, baseline diffs, per-case L1 pass/fail. Fallback axis query-pattern-tag when a cluster < N [fallback-N seed 3, tunable].

C. MIN CLUSTER SIZE: train/holdout activates only at N≥4 (≥2/≥2), random 50/50 with logged seed. Below N=4 → CANNOT-VALIDATE, human-judgment only, never auto-emitted as validated.

D. GENERATION: per cluster LLM proposes K≤3 candidates, each = {hypothesis, diff, target-case set, change-type, blast tier, Type-1 target_prompt / Type-2 scope+scope_key}. CROSS-CLUSTER DEDUP before ranking: near-identical (type+diff, cosine >0.9 [tunable] on the diff embedding) merge into one, union target sets, scored once; NEVER merge across types.

E. ANTI-OVERFIT / REWARD-HACKING: split each failure class into TRAIN (generator sees) / HOLDOUT (blind); a candidate counts only if it moves HOLDOUT cases of the same class to pass. QUARANTINE: a held-out case cannot re-enter train for [N+7 tunable] runs; a BASELINE REFRESH resets all quarantine clocks and re-quarantines the pre-refresh holdout set. EXPLICIT RESIDUALS: (i) on ~25 pairs holdout is weak → the HUMAN APPROVAL GATE is the PRIMARY defense, the split is a secondary signal; (ii) all 25 fixtures share one author → an edit could exploit curator style and pass train+holdout while failing real queries → the reviewer checklist ('fluency vs grounding?') is the guard [OPEN: diversify fixture authorship post-v1].

F. SCORING / RANKING: score each candidate PAIRWISE vs baseline across the WHOLE suite. SEVERITY: L1=3, L2a=2, L2b=1; L3 EXCLUDED from net until calibrated. net = Σ(moved-to-pass × severity) − Σ(regressions × severity). SIGNIFICANCE (permutation-based, no normality assumption): for each candidate compute a permutation p-value — repeatedly (1000× [tunable]) shuffle the per-case candidate-vs-baseline win/loss labels, recompute net, and take p = fraction of permuted |net| ≥ observed. Then apply BENJAMINI-HOCHBERG FDR (q=0.05) across ALL M holdout-passing candidates simultaneously. NO 2σ pre-filter (BH+permutation subsumes it). EMISSION MINIMUMS: net>0 for ALL tiers; additionally HIGH net≥2, MEDIUM ≥1. TIEBREAK: smallest blast tier. EARLY-EXIT: fail holdout → skip whole-suite scoring (holdout stage strictly precedes the whole-suite + FDR stage; no statistical conflict). SUITE-VERSION LOCK: reject cross-version scores. PER-RUN COST BUDGET [~2000 judge calls or $30, tunable]: on exhaustion emit current top-5, flag remaining clusters 'budget-exceeded'.

G. REGRESSION GATE: disqualify (regardless of target wins) any candidate that (a) regresses an L1/L2a gate on a previously-passing case, or (b) drops L2b below the P10 floor. L3 degradation = reviewer flag, not disqualifier. ALL HIGH-tier candidates (global prefix or global note) MUST carry a CROSS-LANE RISK NOTE (fires across all lanes; suite covers only WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS). L1-targeting Type-1 candidates MUST carry a SQL-LOGIC COVERAGE NOTE (few advanced/window pairs exist → elevated uncovered-case risk).

H. FIXTURE-GAP PATH: emit a FIXTURE-GAP NOTE {fixture_id, failure_tag, transcript evidence agent was correct, missing/ambiguous property, proposed change, confidence, origin: generator-run-{date}} → P0 fixture-audit queue, NOT counted vs top-5. Prefer a fixture-gap note over a weak-evidence prompt candidate. LOW confidence = stated confidence <0.6 OR transcript equally supports agent-error vs fixture-gap → surfaced as a count only. Until the P0 expected_answer_facts audit lands, required-fact-missing/omission failures DEFAULT to a fixture-gap note (confidence=LOW); this default is removed post-audit. QUEUE: owner = the loop operator for v1 [OPEN: reassign later]; review cadence every 3 runs or each baseline refresh; HALT TRIGGER — unreviewed fixture-gap count > [M=5 tunable] blocks emission for affected clusters with a FIXTURE-GAP-BACKLOG flag.

I. EMISSION: top-5 by net → morning ranked report → human approval → route to issue/PR/reflection. CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates appear in a SEPARATE report section (do not consume the 5 slots). CONFOUNDER CARD per candidate: cluster N, holdout N, permutation p-value, FDR q-value, pinned model version, baseline freshness, changes-since-baseline, blast tier, cross-lane note, within-domain coverage note (MEDIUM tier), and INTERPRETED FLAGS ([AT VALIDITY FLOOR], [MINIMUM HOLDOUT], [NEXT APPROVAL TRIGGERS BASELINE REFRESH], [NEAR FDR THRESHOLD]).

J. BASELINE / DRIFT: refresh on (model version bump) OR ([5 tunable] approved candidates landed); re-run suite, reset P10 floor + change counter + quarantine clocks + re-estimate permutation null. CUMULATIVE DRIFT GUARD: > [5 tunable] approved prompt edits since refresh → re-capture proposal. DELTA-VS-LAST-BASELINE: at each refresh compare per-case pass vs prior baseline; any newly-regressed case raises a blocking CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION flag (attribution granularity: batch ≤5 candidates, not per-candidate — known limitation). EVAL-CONFIG PREREQS: PINNED model version (not alias), judge temp=0, baseline non-null.

K. LOOP HEALTH: (1) SENTINEL — one human-authored, previously-validated L2a:attribution candidate (L2a chosen because deterministic at temp=0) re-scored every run; LOOP-HEALTH-FAILURE (halt emission) triggers if its net drops run-over-run vs the immediately prior run; keep the full sentinel net time-series; a refresh re-establishes its expected net. (2) GENERATOR MODEL != JUDGE MODEL. (3) reviewer checklist: 'rewarded for fluency rather than grounding?'

OPEN DECISIONS (human input; do NOT block the design lock): fixture-gap queue owner beyond v1; post-v1 fixture-author diversification; v1 acceptance of the metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE blind spot.

WORKED EXAMPLE unchanged: 4 L2a:attribution / engagement / WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS / all L1-PASS → N=4 split 2/2 → Type-2 DOMAIN note ('name the segment on every reported number'), MEDIUM → must fix ≥1 holdout case, pass permutation+BH (q=0.05), not drop L2b below P10, regress no gate, net≥1 → if top-5, emitted with confounder card + reviewer checklist.
args.prior_critique: Round-3 blockers: (A) STATISTICAL METHOD malformed — 2σ pre-filter + BH is invalid; net is discrete at N=25 so CLT/normality fails. REQUIRED FIX: permutation p-values + Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q=0.05 across ALL M candidates, NO 2σ. (B) OPEN DECISIONS needing human input, not more panel rounds: fixture-gap queue owner; single-author-corpus leak mitigation; metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE blind-spot acceptance for v1. These are now defaulted + parked as non-blocking OPEN items. Confirm: (1) stat method now correct; (2) no remaining BLOCKING DESIGN hole; operational/human-input items parked as OPEN must NOT block design consensus.

panel.output:
### [1/3] critic

## Critique

**Summary:** The round-4 design is substantially sound and the round-3 statistical corrections are correctly implemented, but one real FDR violation (BH applied to a data-dependent holdout-filtered M, not M_total) undermines the stated false-discovery guarantee, and a second implementation gap (merged-candidate holdout ambiguity) must be resolved before code is written. Neither blocks design lock, but both must be specified before the first implementation sprint.

---

### (1) Is the generate → score-pairwise-vs-baseline → rank → emit-top-5 loop sound?

**MOSTLY AGREE, one FDR flaw.**

The architecture is sound. Pairwise vs baseline is the correct scoring mode (DL-0020 rationale: judges are more reliable comparatively than absolutely). The permutation null is nonparametric — no normality needed. BH at q=0.05 is appropriate for M simultaneous tests. EARLY-EXIT (holdout gate strictly before whole-suite + FDR) is a clean sequencing choice that avoids statistical conflict. SUITE-VERSION LOCK prevents cross-version score contamination. All round-3 corrections are confirmed present: 2σ pre-filter removed, permutation subsumes it, BH applied across all M candidates simultaneously.

**OBJECT — BH family size is data-dependent (inflated FDR).** Section F: "apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (q=0.05) across ALL M holdout-passing candidates simultaneously." M is the count of candidates that survived the holdout gate — a quantity determined *by the data before BH runs*. BH's FDR guarantee (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995; Theorem 1) requires M to be the pre-specified total number of hypotheses, not a filtered subset. Pre-filtering by holdout outcome before BH is positively correlated with the test statistic (a candidate that improves holdout cases is more likely to have a high whole-suite net); this positive correlation means the BH critical values at M_holdout are too lenient relative to M_total. With typical parameters (K≤3 per cluster, 5-10 daily clusters, ~50% holdout pass rate), M_total ≈ 15-30 and M_holdout ≈ 8-15 — a factor of ~2× too lenient at every rank. Actual FDR could reach 2q = 10% instead of 5%.

**Concrete fix:** Apply BH to M_total (all candidates post-dedup). Holdout-failing candidates receive p=1.0 and are rejected by BH automatically. This preserves the EARLY-EXIT benefit (skip whole-suite scoring for holdout-failers — that path remains for cost efficiency) while making the BH denominator correct. Specifically: run permutation tests only on holdout-passers; assign p=1.0 to holdout-failers; feed all M_total p-values into BH. The only cost is a larger denominator — more stringent significance threshold, which is the correct direction.

---

### (2) Is the train/holdout split a real anti-overfitting guard?

**PARTIAL AGREE — real but weak at minimum cluster size; one implementation gap for merged candidates.**

The split IS a real guard for non-merged, single-cluster candidates: the generator only sees TRAIN cases, the holdout is withheld, quarantine prevents recycling for N+7 runs. The explicit CANNOT-VALIDATE path (N<4) is correct — non-validated candidates are sequestered from the top-5 slots. The design's own EXPLICIT RESIDUALS section honestly names both the ~25-pair weak-holdout residual and the single-author corpus risk.

**OBJECT — 2-case holdout is nearly no signal.** At N=4 (minimum activating cluster), holdout N=2. The holdout gate ("must fix ≥1 holdout case of the same class") on a 2-case set has 3 distinguishable outcomes: fix both, fix one, fix none. Fixing exactly 1 of 2 passes the gate — this is essentially a coin flip on one case. The permutation test on the whole-suite (N=25) is the *real* significance burden; the holdout gate at N=4 contributes almost nothing to anti-overfit beyond "candidate is non-null on at least one unseen case." The MINIMUM HOLDOUT flag is necessary but should be accompanied by an explicit reviewer note (in the confounder card) that the holdout anti-overfit signal is at its absolute floor and human judgment carries the full weight.

**OBJECT — merged-candidate holdout requirement is underspecified (implementation gap).** Section D specifies dedup before ranking (i.e., before scoring, which includes the holdout gate per the staging in §F). When two candidates from clusters A and B are merged, their target-case sets union. But the holdout requirement ("must fix ≥1 holdout case of the same class") becomes ambiguous: "same class" for a merged candidate spanning two different failure-tags is undefined. Does it mean ≥1 from the union? ≥1 from each contributing cluster's holdout? This must be resolved before implementation. The stricter and correct interpretation: for merged candidates, require ≥1 holdout fix from *each* contributing cluster's original holdout set. This prevents a candidate from free-riding on one cluster's holdout while contributing nothing to the other.

**AGREE — single-author corpus (OPEN).** The reviewer checklist ('fluency vs grounding?') is a named guard, not a systematic one. The risk is real — an edit that panics curator phrasing passes train+holdout while failing real queries — but this is correctly identified as OPEN and non-blocking for v1. Acceptable.

---

### (3) Is the ranking metric (net = target-wins×severity − regressions×severity) well-formed and non-gameable?

**MOSTLY AGREE — one structural gaming vector, one clarification on double-counting.**

The metric is well-formed: symmetric severity weighting (same multiplier for wins and regressions), L3 excluded until κ≥0.7 (correct per DL-0022), emission minimums sized by blast tier. The regression gate (§G) as hard pre-filter (not a net penalty) is architecturally correct — it is NOT double-counted with the net because hard-disqualified candidates never reach net scoring. The two-tailed permutation test (|net| ≥ observed) is appropriately conservative for a system that wants low false-positive rate.

**OBJECT — L2b advisory gaming vector.** The regression gate disqualifies regressions of "L1/L2a gate on a previously-passing case" and also disqualifies dropping L2b "below the P10 floor." But between the P10 floor and zero L2b regression, a candidate can degrade L2b without triggering the gate — moving the fleet average down, just not below P10. For L2b weight=1 (lowest severity), this is a low-risk vector. But a candidate that improves a few L1/L2a cases while systematically eroding L2b scores just above P10 could produce a positive net while silently degrading coverage quality. The confounder card includes "within-domain coverage note (MEDIUM tier)" which partially surfaces this. Recommended: add an explicit L2b mean-delta signal to the confounder card (not a gate — keeping it advisory, but surfacing the direction for human reviewers).

**AGREE — emission minimums are well-sized.** HIGH net≥2 and MEDIUM net≥1 set meaningful effect-size floors. A HIGH-tier candidate that only fixes one L2b case (net=1) cannot emit. This is correct — global prefix changes should require larger demonstrated improvements.

---

### (4) Is failure-cluster the right generation unit vs per-case?

**AGREE.**

Per-case generation would create O(N_failures) near-duplicate candidates — the generator would likely produce highly similar candidates for each failure case within the same failure-tag, domain, and lane. Clustering by (L2a failure-tag + domain + lane) is the correct unit because it exposes the pattern (the distribution of failure transcripts) rather than individual instances, which is exactly the information needed to propose a systematic fix rather than a case-specific patch. The CROSS-CLUSTER DEDUP (cosine>0.9 on diff embedding) further consolidates near-duplicate candidates across clusters, maintaining semantic diversity in the emitted top-5.

**OBJECT — embedding model and threshold are unspecified (minor, implementation gap).** Cosine 0.9 on "the diff embedding" requires knowing the embedding space. A token-level embedding (BPE) would conflate semantically distinct but lexically similar diffs; a code-embedding model would be more appropriate for prompt/instruction diffs. Two candidates with identical intent but different surface form could score 0.7 (miss dedup); two candidates that make superficially similar but semantically distinct changes could score 0.92 and incorrectly merge. Minimum spec needed: embedding model name + a 5-10 pair calibration of manual judgments vs cosine scores to validate the threshold.

---

### (5) Attribution: can we actually claim a candidate caused the delta?

**PARTIAL AGREE — correctly scoped for v1, residual risks acknowledged.**

The attribution chain available here is: cluster-targeted generation → holdout generalization check → permutation significance on whole-suite → human approval gate. This chain supports "this candidate is statistically consistent with improvement in the targeted failure class, generalizing beyond training cases" — not "this candidate is the definitive cause of improvement." That's the correct framing for a daily optimization loop.

**AGREE — batch attribution is the honest v1 claim.** Section J acknowledges "attribution granularity: batch ≤5 candidates, not per-candidate — known limitation." This is correct: multiple approved candidates land between baseline refreshes, and the CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION flag operates at the batch level. Per-candidate attribution would require sequential A/B rollout with per-candidate baseline refresh — operationally impractical for a daily loop. Batch attribution is the right v1 posture.

**OBJECT — SENTINEL health signal is slightly misspecified.** Section K: "LOOP-HEALTH-FAILURE triggers if its net drops run-over-run vs the immediately prior run." After a BASELINE REFRESH, the sentinel's expected net is "re-established." The L2a:attribution sentinel at temp=0 should be perfectly deterministic run-over-run on an unchanged baseline. If net drops, the causes are: (a) the baseline absorbed changes that regressed the sentinel's target case, (b) the eval suite version changed, or (c) a judge non-determinism (impossible at temp=0 for L2a). The current design conflates (a) and (c) into one halt signal. Distinguishing them requires comparing the sentinel's target case L2a score directly (was the specific failure case state changed?), not just the net summary. For the rare but non-trivial case where an approved candidate lands that happens to regress the sentinel's target case — a valid and informative regression — the halt fires correctly. AGREE on the overall mechanism; suggest annotating the sentinel's halt reason with "target-case-regression" vs "unexpected-eval-drift" for auditability.

**AGREE — Type-4 retrieval candidates in human-judgment queue.** EVAL-INVISIBLE is an honest acknowledgment that retrieval-path changes cannot be scored through the suite (context is injected directly, bypassing retrieval). Routing these to a human queue with a distinct morning-report line is the correct workaround. Deferring a retrieval-path eval to post-v1 is acceptable — designing an eval that correctly exercises the retrieval step is a non-trivial P1 project in its own right.

---

### Recommended Corrections

| Priority | Section | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Required before implementation** | §F (BH) | Apply BH to M_total candidates; holdout-failers get p=1.0. Preserves EARLY-EXIT for cost; corrects FDR denominator. |
| **Required before implementation** | §D (dedup) | For merged candidates, holdout gate = ≥1 fix from *each* contributing cluster's original holdout set. Add this to the dedup specification. |
| **Recommended** | §E + §I | Confounder card: add explicit L2b mean-delta signal (direction, not gate). Add reviewer note to MINIMUM HOLDOUT flag: "holdout anti-overfit signal is at floor; human approval gate is primary guard for this candidate." |
| **Recommended** | §D | Specify the embedding model for cosine dedup. Calibrate the 0.9 threshold against 5-10 manually-judged near-identical/distinct pairs. |
| **Minor** | §F (budget) | Within same priority tier, process clusters in descending cluster-N order. Documents deterministic ordering under budget pressure. |

---

### Questions (blocking progress)

None that block design lock. The BH fix and merged-candidate holdout spec must be finalized before the first implementation sprint, not before lock.

### [2/3] analyst

## Analysis

### Known — confirmed by codebase and decision log

- **Eval architecture**: DL-0022 locks three layers: L1 (execution-equivalence, gate), L2a (findings grounding, immediate gate, temp=0), L2b (fact-coverage, advisory), L3 (advisory until κ≥0.7). Failure-type tags are `{fabrication|omission|attribution|required-fact-missing}`. (Source: `docs/design/iris-eval-v1-selections.md`)
- **Fixture set**: 25 pairs, entirely ClassDojo product metrics, 9 basic / 13 intermediate / 3 advanced. Eval injects `metric_context + schema_context` directly — **does not exercise retrieval or metric disambiguation**. (Source: `docs/audits/2026-07-28-iris-eval-trustworthiness.md`)
- **Loop scope**: IRIS analyst agent, analysis+findings+SQL, single suite covering `WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS`. (DL-0021)
- **Top-5 cap, portable loop, eval dimensions**: locked in DL-0020/DL-0021/DL-0022.
- **R3 blocker — stat method**: the 2σ pre-filter + BH invalid combination has been replaced with permutation p-values + BH FDR across all M holdout-passing candidates simultaneously, with early-exit at holdout stage before whole-suite scoring. No normality assumption. This is correct.
- **R3 blocker — OPEN items**: fixture-gap queue owner, single-author corpus, metric-disambiguation blind-spot acceptance are now defaulted + parked as non-blocking. Correct disposition.

---

## Per-element verdicts

---

### Q1: Candidate types — are they the right and sufficient levers?

**Type 1 (prompt/instruction) — AGREE with one gap**

The layer-cross check is correct and important: rejecting a `findings_prose` Type-1 when cluster failures are all L1 prevents the most common wrong-layer proposal. The `{target_prompt: sql_generation|findings_prose|system_prefix}` required field is the right granularity for IRIS.

**Gap (not a blocker, but real)**: Neither Type 1 nor any other type cleanly covers *data-assembly pipeline code* — specifically, how executed rows are formatted and injected into the findings prompt. The audit evidence shows IRIS has a pipeline step between SQL execution and findings generation. Attribution failures can originate here (e.g., aggregated totals presented without segment labels, missing time-window headers in the row block) rather than in the prompt text itself. A habit or prompt edit can instruct the agent to "name the segment," but if the data passed to it strips segment columns, the habit is ineffective. This belongs in a Type-5-adjacent "pipeline code" bucket, but Type 5 is currently scoped to "routing/classifier code," which reads as lane-routing logic, not data-assembly. **Concrete fix**: Extend Type 5's definition to explicitly include findings-pipeline code (row formatter, context assembler) with a note that these are HIGH-blast PRs because they affect all downstream findings generation. Or add a Type 6 for it. Either way, keep it as code-PR, not prompt-edit.

**Type 2 (reflections/habits) — AGREE**

This is the primary lever for the worked example and for L2a:attribution failures in general. The scope hierarchy (global/domain/table|user) is well-matched to IRIS's actual failure distribution — attribution errors tend to be domain-specific conventions, not universal. The `landed = merged+approved` gate prevents unapproved habits from appearing in baseline comparisons.

**Type 3 (tool schema/description) — AGREE**

Medium blast, appropriate. For IRIS's MCP-based schema tools, description edits can affect which columns are surfaced. Correctly included.

**Type 4 (retrieval-corpus content) — AGREE with caveat**

The EVAL-INVISIBLE classification is correct: the fixture design (injecting context directly) means retrieval improvements are invisible to the eval signal. Routing these to human-judgment queue is the right v1 call. **The caveat is load**: metric-disambiguation failures — a real and common IRIS failure mode — will accumulate in the human-judgment queue with zero closed-loop leverage indefinitely unless the "roadmap a retrieval-path eval" OPEN item gets a concrete owner and timeline. For v1 this is accepted, but the morning report's "metric-disambiguation failures as a distinct line (count+examples)" is critical — without it, these failures are invisible to the operator.

**Type 5 (routing/classifier code) — AGREE with scope clarification needed**

See Type 1 gap above. Routing failures are real but probably rare relative to L2a failures in the 25-fixture suite.

**Missing lever assessment**: Retrieval/context selection is the largest uncovered lever, correctly identified as EVAL-INVISIBLE. No undiscovered missing type for v1.

---

### Q2: Clustering by (failure-tag + domain) — right unit for IRIS?

**AGREE on structure; OBJECT on query-pattern-tag underspecification**

The `(L2a failure-tag + domain + lane co-filter)` unit is correct in principle. `failure-tag` is the actionable axis — fabrication suggests the agent invented a number; attribution suggests the right number was assigned to the wrong segment/time; omission suggests a required fact wasn't stated. Each maps to a distinct hypothesis class.

**However**: the fallback axis `query-pattern-tag` is undefined in the design. With only 25 fixtures and one effective domain (all ClassDojo metrics), clusters will hit the N<4 fallback frequently. If `query-pattern-tag` values are LLM-generated per-run rather than drawn from a pre-enumerated taxonomy, clustering will be inconsistent across runs — the same fixture could cluster differently depending on how the generator phrases its tag, breaking holdout reproducibility and quarantine tracking.

**Concrete fix**: Define a canonical `query-pattern-tag` taxonomy before the first loop run (e.g., `{date-range, segment-drilldown, comparison, window-function, multi-metric, cohort}`). Seed it from the 25 fixture pair types. LLM assigns tags to fixtures at setup time, not per-run.

**Clustering priority (fabrication/omission by query-pattern first; attribution/required-fact-missing by domain first) — AGREE**

This is domain-correct. Fabrication errors tend to cluster around query complexity (window functions, rolling aggregates), where the agent's SQL execution produces unexpected shapes. Attribution errors cluster around domain conventions (engagement vs revenue metrics have different segment-label norms). The priority inversion is the right call.

---

### Q3: Shared prompt/habit changes — will they help one cluster without breaking others?

**AGREE on mechanism; one structural limitation to flag**

The regression gate (Section G) is the primary defense: any candidate that regresses an L1/L2a gate on a previously-passing case is disqualified. This is the right gate, and the severity-weighted net score (L1=3, L2a=2) means regressions are expensive relative to target wins.

**The structural limitation**: The 25-fixture suite covers only `WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS`. A MEDIUM-tier habit scoped to `WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS` domain is effectively unconstrained by cross-domain regression evidence, because there is no cross-domain evidence. The cross-lane risk note for HIGH-tier candidates (Section G) fires only on globally-scoped changes. For MEDIUM-tier domain-scoped habits — which are the most common type given the worked example — the only cross-lane guard is the reviewer's checklist, not the regression gate. This is correct to call out explicitly in the confounder card's `within-domain coverage note`, but that note is advisory. **Concrete fix**: Add a required flag to MEDIUM-tier domain-scoped candidates when the domain matches the *only* domain in the fixture suite — e.g., `[SOLE-DOMAIN: regression gate has no cross-domain coverage]`. This is different from the existing cross-lane note and sharper. The reviewer needs to know that "MEDIUM tier" does not mean "limited blast" in this specific case.

The `within-domain coverage note` field in the confounder card (Section I) is the right mechanism for this but needs to be populated automatically, not left to the generator's discretion.

---

### Q4: Excluding eval-fixture edits from the generator — correct?

**AGREE. The fixture-gap note path is the concrete routing that makes the exclusion safe.**

Allowing fixture edits through the candidate loop would create a reward-hack path: the generator could propose loosening required-fact definitions or lowering grounding thresholds, those candidates would score positively on the eval, and they'd pass holdout without any real IRIS improvement. The meta-firewall is essential.

**The fixture-gap note path (Section H) is sound with two dependencies:**

1. **The P0 `expected_answer_facts` audit** — Until this lands, `required-fact-missing` failures default to fixture-gap notes (confidence=LOW), which surface only as a count. This means the loop has **zero signal on one entire failure class** until the audit completes. This is correctly modeled as a sequencing dependency, but the design doesn't state what blocks the loop operator from starting runs before the P0 audit. **Concrete fix**: Add an explicit `LOOP-PREREQ` check at emission time: if unreviewed fixture-gap notes of type `required-fact-missing` exceed [threshold] AND the P0 audit is not marked complete, emit a warning-not-halt that reminds the operator the required-fact-missing signal is suppressed.

2. **The HALT trigger at M=5 unreviewed fixture-gap notes** — This is the critical safety valve. Without it, the loop silently generates candidates against bad evidence when fixtures are wrong. The 3-run cadence for queue review is appropriate given the small suite size. **AGREE**.

---

### R3 confirmation: Stat method correctness

**AGREE: stat method is now correct.**

- Permutation p-values with 1000 shuffles on per-case win/loss: no normality assumption, handles discrete net scores on N=25. Correct.
- BH FDR at q=0.05 across all M holdout-passing candidates simultaneously: corrects for multiple comparisons without requiring independence. Correct.
- Early-exit on holdout failure strictly precedes the whole-suite + FDR stage: no statistical conflict. Correct.
- NO 2σ pre-filter: correct removal of the R3 blocker.

### R3 confirmation: Remaining blocking holes

**No remaining BLOCKING DESIGN holes.** The design is lockable. The gaps identified above are:

| Gap | Severity | Blocker? |
|---|---|---|
| Type 5 doesn't cover findings-pipeline code changes | Low–medium | No — v1 can survive; rare failure type |
| `query-pattern-tag` taxonomy undefined | Medium | No — can be defined at setup, before first run |
